claims.claim: The Cardiff Giant was a ten-foot stone man found in a well dig
claims.quote: It was a 10-foot-tall (3.0 m), roughly 3,000 pound purported "petrified man", uncovered on October 16, 1869, by workers digging a well behind the barn of William C. "Stub" Newell, in Cardiff, New York.

claims.claim: There was no need for a well in that spot
claims.quote: He noticed that there was no good reason to try to dig a well in the exact spot the giant had been found.

claims.claim: The discovery took place in Cardiff, New York, on October 16, 1869
claims.quote: uncovered on October 16, 1869, by workers digging a well behind the barn of William C. "Stub" Newell, in Cardiff, New York

claims.claim: The whole length of the giant was 10 feet 4½ inches
claims.quote: The length of the giant was 10 feet 4+1⁄2 inches (3.162 m) and it weighed 2,990 pounds (1,360 kg).

claims.claim: The length of the giant's nose was 6 inches
The width of the giant's palm was 7 inches

claims.claim: The stone for the giant came from a gypsum quarry in Iowa, quarried at Fort Dodge in 1868
claims.quote: In 1868, Hull, accompanied by a man named H. B. Martin, hired men to quarry out a 10-foot-4.5-inch-long (3.2 m) block of gypsum in Fort Dodge, Iowa

claims.claim: The workmen were told the block was for a Lincoln monument in New York
claims.quote: telling them it was intended for a monument to Abraham Lincoln in New York

Date: 1873

claims.claim: The card 3/4 images depict the Fort Dodge gypsum quarry
claims.quote: View in Cardiff Glen, near Fort Dodge, Iowa.

claims.claim: The card 4 image is the verso of a stereocard
The card 4 image bears printed text describing the block going to Chicago, the giant being carved, then shipped to New York and buried in a barn lot
The printed text on the card names George Hull and H. B. Martin
George Hull and H. B. Martin were involved in obtaining the stone block
claims.quote: In 1868, Hull, accompanied by a man named H. B. Martin, hired men to quarry out a 10-foot-4.5-inch-long (3.2 m) block of gypsum in Fort Dodge, Iowa

claims.claim: The block went to Chicago and was carved there
claims.quote: He shipped the block to Edward Burkhardt in Chicago, a German stonecutter. Burkhardt hired two sculptors named Henry Salle and Fred Mohrmann to create the giant.

claims.claim: Yale paleontologist Othniel C. Marsh saw fresh tool marks on soluble gypsum and called it "a most decided humbug"
claims.quote: Yale paleontologist Othniel C. Marsh examined the statue, pointing out that it was made of soluble gypsum, which, had it been buried in its blanket of wet earth for centuries, would not still have fresh tool marks on it (which it did), and termed it "a most decided humbug".

claims.claim: Hull confessed on 10 December 1869
claims.quote: On December 10, 1869, Hull confessed everything to the press

claims.claim: Both giants were ruled fakes in court on 2 February 1870
claims.quote: on February 2, 1870, both giants were revealed as fakes in court

claims.claim: Hull wanted the hoax exposed
claims.quote: confessed proudly that he intended for the hoax to be exposed to reveal the tendency of the Christian community to believe in things too easily

claims.claim: Some preachers/theologians defended the giant's authenticity
claims.quote: Some theologians and preachers, however, defended its authenticity.

claims.claim: It is still not clear whether the Chicago stonecutter who took the job knew what he was carving
claims.quote: While it is not clear if Burkhardt was aware of Hull's intentions, it is reported that they took steps to cover up their work during the carving

claims.claim: Two men were digging the well behind William Newell's barn
claims.quote: Newell hired Gideon Emmons and Henry Nichols, ostensibly to dig a well, and on October 16, 1869, they found the giant.

claims.claim: One of the diggers reportedly said, "I declare, some old Indian has been buried here!"
claims.quote: One of the men reportedly exclaimed, "I declare, some old Indian has been buried here!"

claims.claim: A tent was put up over the giant
claims.quote: The next day, a tent was set up on the discovery site

claims.claim: Newell charged fifty cents for fifteen minutes of viewing
claims.quote: Newell charged each visitor fifty cents for a fifteen-minute session of viewing the giant

claims.claim: Three to five hundred people came per day
claims.quote: The number of visitors went to about three to five hundred per day

claims.claim: Two sculptors shaped the giant behind hung quilts to muffle the noise
claims.quote: Burkhardt hired two sculptors named Henry Salle and Fred Mohrmann to create the giant... putting up quilts to lessen the sound of carving

claims.claim: Sand, sulphuric acid and steel knitting needles were used to give it pores and age
claims.quote: Hull first wiped the giant using a sponge soaked with sand and water. The giant's surface was beaten with steel knitting needles embedded in a board to simulate pores. The giant was also rubbed with sulphuric acid to create a deeper, vintage-like color.

claims.claim: The giant was modelled on George Hull himself
claims.quote: The giant was designed to imitate the form of Hull himself.

claims.claim: George Hull was a tobacconist who lost an argument at a revival meeting about the giants in Genesis 6:4
claims.quote: Hull got into an argument with Reverend Turk and his supporters at a Methodist revival meeting about Genesis 6:4, which states that there were giants who once lived on Earth. Hull, a skeptic, being the minority party, lost the argument.

claims.claim: Andrew D. White was among the geologists who arrived to examine the giant
claims.quote: Andrew D. White, the first president of Cornell University, made a close inspection of the Cardiff Giant.

claims.claim: White noted nobody would dig a well there because there was already a good spring
claims.quote: that there was already a good spring and a stream of water running conveniently to both

claims.claim: Hull sold his interest for $23,000
claims.quote: Eventually, Hull sold his part-interest for $23,000 (equivalent to $586,000 in 2025) to a syndicate of five men headed by David Hannum.

claims.claim: Barnum offered $50,000 and was refused
claims.quote: showman P. T. Barnum offered $50,000 for the giant. When the syndicate refused, he hired a man to model the giant's shape covertly in wax and create a plaster copy.

claims.claim: Barnum had a wax model made in secret and exhibited his own copy
claims.quote: he hired a man to model the giant's shape covertly in wax and create a plaster copy. He displayed his giant in New York
